chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Aban, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the marriage of the Jewish woman and the Christian woman. He said: "It is not suitable for the Muslim to marry the Jewish woman and the Christian woman; rather, permissible from them is the marriage of the 'Balha' (young girl)."

And among its indications is that this is a permission in the state of necessity and when there is no Muslim woman available, and this runs in the same manner as the permission of the dead meat and blood when there is fear for the life.
And that which clarifies what we mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.الْبُلْهِ: The young girl (specific term used in this context)
key_terms.عِنْدَ الْخَوْفِ عَلَى النَّفْسِ: When there is fear for the life
key_terms.نِكَاحُ الْيَهُودِيَّةِ وَالنَّصْرَانِيَ: Marriage of the Jewish and Christian woman

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a Muslim man marrying a Jewish or Christian woman according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Zurara ibn A'yan reports that Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarified the status of marrying Jewish and Christian women, stating that while generally not suitable (or invalid in the primary sense), it is permissible as 'Balha' (young girl) in cases of necessity. This ruling is analogized to the consumption of dead meat or blood when fearing death, indicating a temporary dispensation (ibahah) rather than a permanent permissibility when no Muslim woman is available. This reflects the Shia scholarly view of 'Urfi' or temporary marriage often associated with this context, grounded in the principle of removing hardship.
